ei.title: Chapter 5-13 Analysis: Speech: Communication, Not Performance
ei.subject: 올림포스독해의기본1

fullPassage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about ①<u>making</u> a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is ②<u>judging</u> them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that ③<u>communicate</u> the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him ④<u>seem</u> more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ communicate → communicates
det.analysis:
❌ ① making — concerned about making a mistake에서 전치사 about 뒤 동명사 making 적절

❌ ② judging — the audience is judging them에서 현재진행형 적절

✅ ③ communicate — 원문은 communicates. 선행사가 a well-thought-out address(단수)인 주격 관계대명사 that절의 동사이므로 3인칭 단수 communicates가 옳음. communicate(원형)는 수 일치 위반 ←정답

❌ ④ seem — make her or him seem more human에서 사역동사 make + 목적어 + 원형부정사 seem 적절
det.tip: 관계대명사 that의 선행사(address, 단수) → 동사 communicates

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is ①<u>that</u> they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every ②<u>misstated</u> word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not ③<u>like</u> judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him ④<u>to seem</u> more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to seem → seem
det.analysis:
❌ ① that — The biggest reason is that they view...에서 보어절을 이끄는 접속사 that 적절

❌ ② misstated — every misstated word에서 과거분사가 형용사로 명사 word 수식, 적절

❌ ③ like — audiences are not like judges에서 '~와 같은'을 뜻하는 전치사 like 적절

✅ ④ to seem — 원문은 seem. by making her or him seem more human에서 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어는 원형부정사 seem이어야 함. to seem은 사역동사 구문 위반 ←정답
det.tip: make + 목적어 + 원형부정사(seem): to부정사 불가

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they ①<u>view</u> speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection ②<u>which</u> every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that ③<u>communicates</u> the speaker's ideas clearly and ④<u>directly</u>. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② which → in which
det.analysis:
❌ ① view — they view speechmaking as a performance에서 주어 they에 대한 동사 view 적절

✅ ② which — 원문은 in which. a scale of absolute perfection in which every word will count against them에서 관계사절이 완전한 절(every word will count against them)이므로 '전치사+관계대명사(in which)'가 필요. which만 쓰면 전치사 in이 사라져 부적절 ←정답

❌ ③ communicates — a well-thought-out address that communicates에서 단수 선행사에 맞춘 단수 동사 communicates 적절

❌ ④ directly — communicates the ideas clearly and directly에서 부사 clearly와 병렬을 이루는 부사 directly 적절
det.tip: 완전한 절 앞 → 전치사+관계대명사(in which) / 불완전한 절 앞 → which

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of ①<u>communication</u>. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute ②<u>perfection</u> in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a ③<u>virtuoso</u> performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually ④<u>reduce</u> a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ reduce(줄이다) → enhance(높이다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① communication — 연설을 공연이 아닌 '의사소통(communication)' 행위로 본다는 원문 맥락에 적절

❌ ② perfection — 청중이 절대적 '완벽함(perfection)'의 기준으로 평가한다는 맥락에 적절

❌ ③ virtuoso — 청중이 '(대가의) 화려한 기교(virtuoso) 공연'을 찾는 것이 아니라는 원문 맥락에 적절

✅ ④ reduce — 원문은 enhance. 뒤에서 실수가 연설가를 더 인간적으로 보이게 한다고 했으므로, 실수가 매력을 '높인다(enhance)'가 자연스러움. reduce(줄이다)는 의미가 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: enhance appeal(매력을 높이다) ↔ reduce appeal(매력을 줄이다)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a ①<u>mistake</u> in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of ②<u>absolute</u> perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas ③<u>vaguely</u> and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's ④<u>appeal</u> by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ vaguely(모호하게) → clearly(명확하게)
det.analysis:
❌ ① mistake — 연설에서 '실수(mistake)'하는 것을 걱정한다는 원문 맥락에 적절

❌ ② absolute — '절대적(absolute)' 완벽함의 기준이라는 원문 맥락에 적절

✅ ③ vaguely — 원문은 clearly. 좋은 연설은 생각을 '명확하게(clearly)' 그리고 직접적으로 전달한다는 맥락이므로, vaguely(모호하게)는 directly(직접적으로)와 모순되어 부적절 ←정답

❌ ④ appeal — 실수가 연설가의 '매력(appeal)'을 높일 수 있다는 원문 맥락에 적절
det.tip: communicate clearly(명확하게 전달) ↔ vaguely(모호하게)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for __________, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 청중은 '화려한 기교의 공연(a virtuoso performance)'을 찾는 것이 아니라 명확한 의사 전달을 찾는다
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장은 not ___, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates ideas clearly 구조로, 빈칸에는 '잘 준비된 연설'과 대비되는 부정적 대상이 와야 함.

✅ ① a virtuoso performance (대가의 화려한 기교 공연) — 앞 문장의 performance(공연) 대 communication(의사소통) 대비, 그리고 judges in a violin recital 비유와 연결되어 정답 ←정답

❌ ② an honest apology (정직한 사과) — 사과라는 개념은 지문에 등장하지 않음

❌ ③ a detailed script (상세한 대본) — 대본 준비 여부는 논점이 아님

❌ ④ a personal connection (개인적 유대) — 오히려 뒤 문장의 more human과 통하는 긍정적 요소라 대비 대상으로 부적절
det.tip: not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than __________. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 연설을 '공연'이 아니라 '의사소통 행위(an act of communication)'로 보아야 한다는 글 전체의 핵심
det.analysis:
빈칸은 view speechmaking as a performance rather than ___ 구조로, performance(공연)와 대비되는 개념이 필요.

❌ ① a competitive sport (경쟁 스포츠) — 스케이팅 대회 비유가 있으나 연설의 본질로 제시되지 않음

✅ ② an act of communication (의사소통 행위) — 글 전체가 연설을 공연이 아닌 의사소통으로 보라고 주장하므로 정답 ←정답

❌ ③ a test of memory (기억력 시험) — 암기 여부는 지문의 논점이 아님

❌ ④ a form of entertainment (오락의 한 형태) — 오락은 오히려 performance 쪽에 가까워 대비 개념으로 부적절
det.tip: performance(공연) rather than an act of communication(의사소통 행위)

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates ideas clearly
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원문 not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates clearly와 일치 ←정답

❌ ② 청중이 완벽함 기준으로 감점한다는 것은 연설가가 '느끼는' 오해일 뿐, 실제 청중의 태도가 아님

❌ ③ 청중은 바이올린 심사위원 같지 않다고 했으므로 완벽한 기교 요구는 반대

❌ ④ 실수가 오히려 매력을 높일 수 있다(enhance appeal)고 했으므로 '언제나 신뢰를 떨어뜨린다'는 반대
det.tip: 화려한 기교(X) → 명확한 의사 전달(O)

ch: 청중은 화려한 기교보다 명확하게 전달되는 연설을 원한다.
청중은 사소한 실수도 완벽함의 기준으로 반드시 감점한다.
훌륭한 연설가는 바이올린 연주자처럼 완벽한 기교를 보여야 한다.
연설 중의 실수는 언제나 연설가의 신뢰를 떨어뜨린다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 실수를 걱정하는 이유는 연설을 '의사소통'이 아니라 '공연'으로 보기 때문 → 선지 ③이 반대로 서술됨
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문 They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection과 일치

❌ ② 원문 audiences are not like judges in ... an ice-skating contest와 일치

✅ ③ 원문은 view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. 걱정의 이유는 연설을 '공연'으로 보기 때문이므로 '의사소통 행위로 보기 때문'은 정반대 서술 ←정답(불일치)

❌ ④ 원문 an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal과 일치
det.tip: 걱정의 원인 = 연설을 공연으로 봄(performance), 의사소통(communication) 아님

ch: 어떤 사람들은 청중이 절대적 완벽함의 기준으로 자신을 평가한다고 느낀다.
연설 청중은 아이스스케이팅 대회의 심판과는 다르다.
사람들이 연설 실수를 걱정하는 주된 이유는 연설을 의사소통 행위로 보기 때문이다.
한두 개의 실수가 오히려 연설가의 매력을 높일 수 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human
det.analysis:
❌ ① 몸짓을 완벽하게 기억한다는 내용은 지문에 없음(완벽함 감점은 연설가의 오해)

❌ ② 청중은 심사위원과 다르다고 했으므로 심사위원처럼 대하라는 것은 반대

det.tip: seem more human → enhance appeal(호소력 상승)

ch: 청중은 연설가의 모든 몸짓을 완벽하게 기억하려 애쓴다.
연설가는 청중을 바이올린 심사위원처럼 대해야 한다.
잘 준비된 연설보다 화려한 기교가 더 높이 평가된다.
연설가가 더 인간적으로 보이면 청중에게 호소력이 커질 수 있다.

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 연설을 완벽한 공연이 아니라 의사소통으로 바라보아야 한다는 것이 글의 주제
det.analysis:
❌ ① why public speaking requires flawless technical skills (연설이 완벽한 기교를 요구하는 이유) — 글은 완벽한 기교가 필요 없다고 주장하므로 반대

✅ ② viewing a speech as communication rather than a flawless performance (연설을 완벽한 공연이 아닌 의사소통으로 보기) — 실수 걱정의 원인과 해법을 관통하는 핵심 주제 ←정답

det.analysis:

ch: It Is Communication, Not a Flawless Show

questions.passage: One of the biggest reasons people are concerned about making a mistake in a speech is that they view speechmaking as a performance rather than an act of communication. They feel the audience is judging them against a scale of absolute perfection in which every misstated word or awkward gesture will <u>count against them</u>. But speech audiences are not like judges in a violin recital or an ice-skating contest. They are not looking for a virtuoso performance, but for a well-thought-out address that communicates the speaker's ideas clearly and directly. Sometimes an error or two can actually enhance a speaker's appeal by making her or him seem more human.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 count against them이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: count against ~ = ~에게 불리하게 작용하다. 사소한 실수 하나까지 연설가에게 불리하게 평가된다는 의미
det.analysis:
밑줄은 every misstated word or awkward gesture will count against them 문맥으로, 완벽함의 기준에서 모든 사소한 흠이 불리하게 작용한다는 뜻.

❌ ① Every mistake will be quickly forgotten (실수가 빨리 잊힐 것) — 불리하게 남는다는 원 의미와 반대

❌ ② Small errors will be counted and rewarded fairly (사소한 실수가 공정히 보상받을 것) — 보상이 아니라 감점 개념

✅ ③ Even the smallest flaw will be judged negatively against the speaker (아주 작은 흠까지 연설가에게 불리하게 평가될 것) — count against(불리하게 작용하다)의 함축과 일치 ←정답

❌ ④ The audience will help the speaker fix each error (청중이 실수 교정을 도울 것) — 지문에 없는 내용
det.tip: count against them = 그들에게 불리하게 작용하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:

❌ ① sound more professional (더 전문적으로 들리다) — 실수와 전문성은 오히려 상충

❌ ② look more confident (더 자신감 있어 보이다) — 자신감은 지문의 초점이 아님

det.tip: error → seem more human → enhance appeal
